root_cause.text: `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` in the FUSE dentry cache logic could read `dentry->d_time` before it was initialized because newly allocated dentries from `__d_alloc()`/`lookup_open()` were not given an initial epoch value by `fuse_dentry_init()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly adds `dentry->d_time = 0;` in `fuse_dentry_init()` with the comment that this initializes the epoch so the dentry is invalid against `fc->epoch`, and the CVE notes KMSAN reported an uninit-value in `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` when `lookup_open()` called `d_revalidate()` on a dentry created by `__d_alloc()` without `->d_time` initialized.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize new FUSE dentries with a stale epoch so they are invalidated correctly against the filesystem epoch.
intent_record.what: In fuse_dentry_init(), a new comment was added and dentry->d_time is explicitly initialized to 0 after dentry->d_fsdata is set.
intent_record.how: This makes newly created FUSE dentries start with an epoch value that is guaranteed to be older than fc->epoch, so they will be treated as invalid on comparison until properly refreshed.

grouping_result.intent: Initialize new FUSE dentries with a stale epoch so they are invalidated correctly against the filesystem epoch.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it initializes newly allocated FUSE dentries with an epoch value so `fuse_dentry_revalidate()` does not read an uninitialized `dentry->d_time`.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix initialization path for a new FUSE dentry, but it does not assign any initial epoch/time value to the dentry. As a result, later dentry revalidation could read dentry->d_time before it had been initialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the pre-fix FUSE dentry initialization statement. It sets private data but leaves dentry->d_time uninitialized, which allows fuse_dentry_revalidate() to later read an uninitialized epoch/time value.
